notes.text: For more than 8, brown the eggplant in two batches so it doesn't crowd the pot, and use your biggest pot.

move.title: A pile of cubes becomes a stew
move.body: Dicing means cutting food into cubes that are all about the same size. Today you'll dice five different vegetables, brown some of them, and let them all simmer together into ratatouille, a French vegetable stew.

why.title: Planks, sticks, cubes
why.body: Every dice works the same way. Cut flat planks, cut the planks into sticks, then cut across the sticks. Each cut across a row of sticks makes a whole row of cubes, and if the planks and sticks were even, the cubes are too.

why.title: Round things get a flat side
why.body: Eggplant and zucchini are round, and round food rolls under a knife. Cut them in half the long way first, then lay the flat side on the board. Now they sit still for every cut that follows.

why.title: Eggplant is a sponge
why.body: Raw eggplant is full of tiny air pockets, and it soaks up oil fast. The pan will look dry after a minute. Don't add more oil. Keep cooking, and as the eggplant softens it lets some of the oil back out and turns golden.

why.title: Low and slow, then lid off
why.body: Small, lazy bubbles cook the vegetables gently, so they turn soft without breaking into mush. With the lid on, the steam stays in and everything softens. With the lid off at the end, water escapes as steam, and the juices cook down into a thick sauce.

wrong.sign: The pot looks dry and the eggplant is sticking
wrong.fix: Turn the heat down a little and stir. Add a spoonful of water, not oil, to loosen the stuck bits.
Leave the lid off and simmer a few more minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens.
It still tastes good. Next time, keep the bubbles small and cut the cubes a little bigger.

wrong.sign: Some cubes are soft and others still hard
wrong.fix: The cubes were different sizes. Cook a few more minutes until the big ones catch up.

quiz.q: The eggplant soaked up all the oil and the pot looks dry. What do you do?
quiz.explain: As the eggplant softens, it lets some oil back out.

quiz.q: Why do you take the lid off near the end?
choices: So the juices cook down and thicken
quiz.explain: With the lid off, water escapes as steam, and the sauce thickens.

steps.text: Rinse all the vegetables in the colander and dry them.

Cut the ends off the eggplant. Cut it in half the long way and lay each half flat side down. Cut it into planks about ¾ inch thick, cut the planks into sticks, then cut across the sticks to dice it into cubes. Put them in the medium bowl.
steps.tip: These cubes are bigger than a pea, about the size of a game die. Eggplant shrinks a lot as it cooks.

steps.text: Cut the ends off the zucchini. Cut each one in half the long way, lay it flat side down, and cut it into long sticks. Line the sticks up and cut across them into cubes the same size as the eggplant. Put them in the large bowl.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front.

steps.text: Cut the top and bottom off each pepper. Stand it up, cut down one side, and open it out flat. Cut away the seeds and white ribs. Lay it skin side down, cut it into strips, then cut across the strips into small squares. Add them to the large bowl.
steps.tip: Skin side down, so the knife doesn't slip on the shiny skin.

steps.text: Cut the onion in half through the root and peel it, leaving the root on. Lay each half flat side down, cut strips toward the root without cutting through it, then cut across the strips to dice it. Add it to the large bowl.
steps.tip: The root holds the layers together while you cut.

steps.text: Peel the garlic and mince it into tiny bits. Put it in the small bowl.
Cut each tomato into quarters, lay them skin side down, and dice them, juice and seeds and all. Scrape them onto the garlic.
steps.tip: Keep the seeds and juice this time. In a stew they cook down into the sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil for the eggplant in the pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the eggplant and {qty:salt} salt. Cook, stirring every minute or so, until the cubes are soft and golden at the edges.
steps.look: Golden edges, and the cubes squash easily when you press one with the spoon.

steps.text: Spoon the eggplant back into the medium bowl.
Add the oil for the stew to the pot, then the onion, pepper, and zucchini. Cook, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and see-through.
Push the vegetables to the sides. Put the thyme and oregano in the empty middle of the pot and stir them into the oil for a few seconds, then stir everything together.
steps.tip: Dried herbs wake up when they touch hot oil. You'll smell it right away.

steps.text: Add the eggplant back, with the tomatoes and garlic, the stew's salt, and the pepper. Stir and let it come up to bubbling.
Turn the heat down to low and put the lid on. Let it simmer, stirring once or twice.
steps.look: Small, lazy bubbles that pop now and then.
steps.tip: Lift the lid away from you, so the steam doesn't hit your face.

steps.text: Take the lid off and keep simmering, stirring now and then, until the juices cook down and thicken.
steps.look: A thick, glossy sauce, with no pool of thin liquid at the bottom.

steps.text: Turn off the stove. Taste a little on a clean spoon, after blowing on it, and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
steps.tip: Stews are very hot inside. Let a spoonful cool for a moment before tasting.

steps.text: Tear the basil leaves over the top if you're using them. Serve in bowls, with slices of baguette for scooping up the sauce.
steps.tip: Ratatouille tastes even better the next day, warmed up or at room temperature.

eggplant.text: Trim the eggplant. Cut ½-inch planks, ½-inch batons, then ½-inch cubes. Put them in the medium bowl.
eggplant.look: Cubes ½ inch on every side.

zucchini.text: Trim the zucchini and cut it into ½-inch cubes the same way, discarding the seedy core if it's soft. Put them in the large bowl.

pepper.text: Open the peppers flat, remove the ribs and seeds, and cut ½-inch squares, skin side down. Add them to the large bowl.

onion.text: Cut the onion into a ¼-inch small dice. Add it to the large bowl.

garlic.text: Mince the garlic fine. Put it in the small bowl.

tomatoes.text: Core the tomatoes, quarter them, and cut them into a ½-inch dice, keeping the juice and seeds. Add them to the garlic.

taste.text: Turn off the heat. Taste and adjust the salt.

serve.text: Tear the basil over the top. Serve with sliced baguette.
